_doc: The classification vocabulary for brokerage_transactions rows, and the
single source of truth for it: parser_common.py validates against this
file, OrbySystems' pkg/ingest reads the same file out of the embedded scripts
tree to build its SQL, and tests/test_transaction_vocabulary.py fails CI
when a bundled parser emits a word that is not here.
WHY IT EXISTS. Money entering or leaving an account has to be
recognisable as such, because every growth figure is computed net of it.
Detection used to be a two-word allowlist (action IN ('Deposit',
'Withdrawal')) plus one convention (transaction_type = 'internal_transfer')
that four parsers happened to follow. A parser calling a contribution
'Contribution', 'Rollover' or 'Journal' had that money silently counted
as investment gain - no error, no warning, a portfolio that appears to
have earned its own deposits.
THE TWO FIELDS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING.
action           - the ISSUER'S OWN WORD, free text, for display. CSV
parsers pass the export's column through verbatim,
which is legitimate and which is why this field
cannot have a closed vocabulary.
transaction_type - the MACHINE-READABLE CLASSIFICATION, closed. If it
is set at all it must be one of transaction_types
below, and parse() rejects anything else by name.
SO: classify with transaction_type. The action lists below are a safety
net for rows that carry no classification - they are a convenience, not
the guarantee. The guarantee is that an unrecognised word is REPORTED
(OrbySystems warns at import) and, for a bundled parser, FAILS CI.
_flows_doc: One entry per class of money movement. transaction_type is the value a
parser SHOULD set; actions are issuer words that mean the same thing and
are honoured when no transaction_type is present.
direction: 'in' / 'out' / 'sign' - 'sign' means the row's own amount
decides, which is what a two-way class like a cash sweep needs.
external: true when the money crosses the portfolio boundary. An
internal transfer between two of the user's own accounts nets to zero
across the portfolio and must not count as a contribution to it.
_non_flow_actions_doc: THE CLOSURE RULE, which is what the CI check and OrbySystems' import guard
a row that sets transaction_type is CLASSIFIED - its action is free
prose and nothing checks it. A corporate-action row's action is lifted
verbatim out of the statement ('Merger Out', 'Assigned Out', whatever
the issuer printed), which is exactly why it must not be checked.
a row that sets NO transaction_type is classified by its action alone,
so that action must appear either in a flows[].actions list above or
in non_flow_actions below. A word in neither list is a word nobody has
looked at: CI fails for a bundled parser, and OrbySystems warns at import for
So this list is not a catalogue of everything a statement can say. It is
the set of unclassified words we have already examined and decided are
not money movement. The way to stay out of it is to set transaction_type.
_non_flow_classes_doc: What each examined non-flow word MEANS, on a row that carries no
transaction_type - the non-flow counterpart of flows[].actions.
OrbySystems resolves every brokerage_transactions row to one value of
own transaction_type when it sets one, otherwise the class its action is
listed under here or in flows[], otherwise ''. Income, tax lots, option
and performance figures read that resolved class and never the action
word, so 'Qualified Dividend' with transaction_type 'dividend' counts as a
dividend exactly as an unclassified 'Dividend' does.
'Margin Interest' is listed under fee, not interest: it is a charge the
account paid, which v_period_return books as a charge, and counting it as
interest would report it as negative income.
Every word here must also be in non_flow_actions. A word that is there
and in no class here ('Dividend/Interest', 'Return Of Capital') is known,
so it raises no warning, but nothing that needs a class counts it.
_corporate_action_events_doc: A corporate_action row's action is the issuer's own label ('Expired Out',
'Option Expiration', 'Assigned Out') and its subtype is its direction
('In' / 'Out', which the securities table's merger links rely on), so
what the event WAS can only be read from the label. A row whose
transaction_type is corporate_action, or which carries none, is an event
below when any whole word of its action, compared case-insensitively, is
one of that event's words (v_scoped_transactions.corporate_event). The
option recipes use 'expired' and 'assigned' to find the row that ended a
contract. 'reverse_split' is listed before 'split' deliberately - a
label like 'Reverse Stock Split' contains the word 'split' too, and the
first event whose word list matches wins, so 'reverse' has to be checked
first or a reverse split would always read as an ordinary one.
pkg/ingest/tax_lots.go's applySplitRatio is what actually turns one of
these two into a lot adjustment, not just a label. Words are lower-case
_corporate_events_doc: THE CLASSIFICATION OF A CORPORATE ACTION. Every brokerage_transactions row
whose transaction_type is corporate_action sets corporate_event to one of
corporate_events below. Like transaction_type it is closed: parse() rejects
any other value by name. The row's action stays the issuer's own word, for
display; nothing downstream matches on it.
A parser sets what the STATEMENT SHOWS and never guesses a cause.
Stated - the statement names the event:
split, reverse_split, spinoff, merger_in, merger_out,
conversion_in, conversion_out (a ticker or CUSIP change),
expired, assigned, exercised (an option contract ended), cash_in_lieu
Observed - only the shape is printed, the cause is not:
share_distribution   shares of a security arrive with no cash and no
stated reason (Fidelity prints a split this way)
share_exchange_in / share_exchange_out
shares move between securities with no stated
event
other                  anything else (an adjustment, a lending credit).
An observed kind is resolved after import, from the surrounding data (the
adjacent holdings snapshots) or by the user; that answer is stored apart
from this field, so re-parsing a statement never overwrites it. Setting an
observed kind is always right when unsure; setting a stated one the
statement does not state is not.
A word in two institutions' statements is therefore never the key: the
same bare 'Distribution' is share_distribution from a statement that
prints no cash, and a cash distribution (an RMD) is transaction_type
distribution, a different field entirely.
_corporate_event_directions_doc: The direction a corporate_event implies for the security the row is about,
as the row's subtype carries it ('In' arriving, 'Out' leaving). A row whose
subtype is In or Out and contradicts its event is rejected by parse(): the
event is authoritative, subtype is a display hint. Events not listed here
(split, reverse_split, cash_in_lieu, other) have no fixed direction.
_corporate_event_labels_doc: Words in an action label that name a STATED event, for a parser that
lifts the issuer's label (parser_common.label_event). Compared as
lower-case letter runs, whole words, first match wins - so 'reverse' is
listed before 'split'. 'merger' and 'conversion' have no direction of their own: they become
merger_in / merger_out and conversion_in / conversion_out from the row's subtype (In / Out).
